programmes.d: A quadriplegic woman loved by her community is found dead in an Orlando park 150ft from her motorized wheelchair. Children find her lifeless body face down in the sand.
Jerra Kirby, who’s visiting family in Orlando, has suddenly passed out at a theme park wave pool and the paramedics are trying desperately to revive her.
Chris Schaffer has not been seen or heard from in five days. Finally, his friends find him dead and decomposed in the driver’s seat of his van.
Ricky Hawthorne, a middle-aged man with a history of AIDS, arrives at his local hospital complaining of chest pains. Doctors perform extensive tests on him but find nothing wrong and release him.
Teenagers stumble across a horrifying car fire on the side of a desolate stretch of roadway. When the police arrive, they pull severely burned human remains from the driver’s seat.
A retired military officer is found dead in his own backyard during a freak ice storm in San Antonio, Texas.
Four new farmers. One new host.
One lucky lady from each farm heads up early to enjoy a solo date with her farmer.
After some farmers couldn't decide who to send home, their best friends are called in to help.
The farmers and their ladies head to Tennessee for a barn dance.
At the barn dance, love is in the air, but a dramatic departure shakes up the night.
The farmers receive a letter, revealing that their moms have chosen a new lady for them to meet.
A man is impaled in the abdomen by a stiletto heel. A seemingly healthy outdoorsman has a series of seizures.
Three patients sneak their pets into the hospital, causing pandemonium in the ER.
A patient appears to be hallucinating and sends the ER staff on a wild-goose chase around the hospital.
A surfer is impaled between the legs by the fin of his surfboard.
A live boa constrictor wrapped around a man's arm is biting his wrist and won't let go.

A hospital worker feels like she's dying, but doctors can find nothing wrong; a physician's young son is a patient in her own ER, demanding her attention while she's trying to treat others; a woman's hobby of wild mushroom picking sends her to the ER.

A man is rushed to the ER, apparently clawed by a tiger, but he won't reveal the real source of his injuries; a patient says he's been shot in the head, but the bullet is nowhere to be found; a woman is brain dead, but one doctor thinks she can be saved.
More than 1,000lbs of dry wall crush onto a young boy's chest, stopping blood circulation to his vital organs. Doctors fear the worst.
Gripping tales of medical emergencies. Doctors must look after their own when a psychotic gunman enters the hospital and starts shooting staff. Dr May is shot in the head, but can his colleague save.
A mother and son are brought in after a horrific car accident. The son was not wearing a seat belt during the crash and was ejected from the car.
A police man is struck by a speeding driver seeking revenge, which may leave him with no legs. A team of doctors try and save the officer's life.
Snake-bite expert Dr Sean Bush faces his own nightmare when his wife calls to tell him a venomous rattlesnake has just bitten their two-year-old son.
During her career as a medical examiner, Dr. G has autopsied thousands of murder victims. In this episode, Dr. G shares her most memorable case.
Dr. G reviews a woman's medical records and learns that she suffered from an auto-immune disease called lupus, which might have something to do with her death.
Motor vehicle fatalities account for many of the cases that come into the morgue. Dr. G offers expertise as to how to get behind the wheel and not wind up on a steel table.
When Dr. G receives Lea Conrad's body, she suspects the woman may have died from an antihistamine overdose. Then, Dr. G learns that Lea was being treated for lupus.
